title: Interactive Routing Policy Builder: region/tier selection, variant fallback previews
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Ship an interactive, customer-configurable policy editor in Console that lets teams define routing rules by region, account tier, and graceful fallback to model variants. The editor should validate policies, show a live preview of routing outcomes for sample traffic, and surface warnings about potential SLA/cost impacts.

Scope:
- Visual policy builder with blocks for: region selection, tier-based routing (e.g., enterprise vs standard), and fallback chains of model variants (primary -> degraded -> fallback).
- Syntactic + semantic validation that prevents unsafe policies (e.g., routing to unsupported region/model combos, infinite fallback loops).
- Traffic preview sandbox that simulates a configurable sample of requests and shows where each request would route and expected latency/cost buckets.
- Persisted policy JSON that can be pinned to routes and included in rollout plans.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Backend runtime routing optimizations (handled in ENG-2187).
- Full A/B experiment framework for policies (follow-up).

Why this matters: Customers run multi-region and tiered deployments and need predictable routing behavior for latency/cost/reliability trade-offs. Current Console lacks an easy way to author and sanity-check these policies, causing support tickets and misconfigurations for dedicated/private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Editor UI allows composing rules for region, tier, and fallback variants and saves as a named policy
Editor performs real-time validation and surfaces clear error/warning messages for invalid combos
Preview simulator shows per-sample routing decisions with metadata (selected region, model variant, estimated latency and cost bucket)
Policies export/import as JSON compatible with runtime API contract (see attachments)
Beta rollout with 3 pilot customers and no critical regressions for 2 weeks
activity: 2025-02-15: Kickoff meeting with Design (Maya Chen), Eng (Eli Wang), and Product (Ava Patel). Agreed scope and success metrics (latency SLO adherence, config error reduction).
2025-02-20: Design spike: two concepts — block-based canvas vs form-driven stepper. Design favors block canvas for expressivity; Product asked for a simplified stepper for first iteration.
2025-02-24: Eng feasibility review (ENG-2187 owners): confirmed runtime supports model variants and region metadata; need a validation API endpoint from backend (ENG-2203).
2025-02-27: PM/Design review: added explicit warning when policy allows cross-region fallback for data-restricted customers. Marked as security_review_required.
2025-03-03: Prototype demo in Console staging showing stepper UI + preview table (internal link in attachments). Engineering requested agreed schema v1 for persisted policy JSON.
2025-03-05: Design sign-off on wording for validation messages. Engineering began API work and initial PR created (see attachments). Next: QA test plan and pilot onboarding checklist.
